sentences: A single black square inside a white border is all there is, yet this is one of the most famous paintings of the twentieth century.
With it the Russian avant-garde artist Kazimir Malevich launched Suprematism in 1915, calling the work the 'zero point of painting'.
The black square first appeared in 1913, in his stage designs for the Futurist opera Victory over the Sun.

At the Last Futurist Exhibition 0,10 in Petrograd in 1915 he hung it high in the corner of the room, the place a Russian home reserves for its icon, staging a head-on collision between Orthodox tradition and the new art.
The web of cracks on its surface is partly the result of neglect: under Stalin his work was banned, and the painting was not exhibited again until the 1980s.
In 2015 X-rays revealed two earlier compositions hidden beneath the black paint, along with a handwritten inscription.
Malevich later painted the image three more times, and two of those versions are also in the Tretyakov Gallery.
